newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia arrests Timorese for attacking police.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia arrests Timorese for attacking police.

text.p: Indonesian police have detained 34 youths from East Timor for ransacking a police station and attacking two police officers in neighbouring West Timor, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.

The agency quoted chief of the Belu police station in West Timor, Lieutenant-Colonel Nyoman Sumantha, as saying on Tuesday police still had the young men in detention. He said they went on a rampage after being reprimanded for overpacking a bus.
"We are still questioning them and searching for seven others," Sumantha was quoted as saying.

He said the men attacked the Betun police station, 298 km (186 miles) east of Kupang, capital of West Timor, after being told by Betun police chief Sergeant-Major Y.P. Panie not to overpack the bus on February 10.
Sumantha said the young men, from Kovalima regency in East Timor, had visited Betun by bus to settle a dispute with local youths after a brawl at a wedding party.

He said the men returned to Kovalima but came back later that day to attack the police station, injuring Panie and his deputy. Antara gave no other details. West Timor, part of the East Nusa Tenggara province, is located on the western half of Timor island.
Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
